$comment: Controls register: every automatic check that enforces the rulebook (metamodel), where it runs, where its outcome is recorded and what monitors it. Rendered into docs/controls-register.md.
monitoring_today: Continuous integration only: every push and pull request runs all controls on the example data. There is no production monitoring, alerting or dashboard yet — that arrives with ingestion of real data (ROADMAP).

controls.control: Every record is a known, concrete kind of thing (not abstract, not an artefact), of its dataset's layer
controls.outcome_recorded_in: command output (ERROR lines); graph store load record — a `rejected` entry listing every error
controls.monitored_by: GitHub Actions `validate.yml` on every push and pull request (Python 3.10–3.12); a failure marks the commit red; tests/test_graph.py, tests/test_conformance.py

controls.control: Attribute types, allowed values, required attributes, references and natural keys
controls.outcome_recorded_in: command output (ERROR / WARN lines); graph store load record
controls.monitored_by: GitHub Actions `validate.yml` on every push and pull request (Python 3.10–3.12); a failure marks the commit red; tests/test_conformance.py

controls.control: Only allowed link kinds between the right record types; link-count limits
controls.outcome_recorded_in: command output; graph store load record
controls.monitored_by: GitHub Actions `validate.yml` on every push and pull request (Python 3.10–3.12); a failure marks the commit red; tests/test_graph.py, tests/test_conformance.py

controls.control: Each record matches its per-entity JSON Schema (the format an adapter writes)
controls.runs: any JSON Schema tool; the test suite
controls.monitored_by: GitHub Actions `validate.yml` on every push and pull request (Python 3.10–3.12); a failure marks the commit red; tests/test_conformance.py (physical model)

controls.control: A cross-layer link is one of the 9 types, between the right kinds of record, adjacent layers, no artefact ends
controls.monitored_by: GitHub Actions `validate.yml` on every push and pull request (Python 3.10–3.12); a failure marks the commit red (sdem-validate --strict on every registry)

controls.control: Approval needs a reviewer, a date, the evidence kinds the link type requires, and for BIAN-anchored types a BIAN release and identifier
controls.monitored_by: GitHub Actions `validate.yml` on every push and pull request (Python 3.10–3.12); a failure marks the commit red

controls.control: Approved links are never edited; only allowed status changes
controls.monitored_by: GitHub Actions `validate.yml` on every push and pull request (Python 3.10–3.12); a failure marks the commit red (sdem-diff --git HEAD~1)

controls.control: Both ends of every approved link exist, at the stated version, of the right type
controls.outcome_recorded_in: command output; graph store load record
controls.monitored_by: GitHub Actions `validate.yml` on every push and pull request (Python 3.10–3.12); a failure marks the commit red

controls.control: The engine finds the right links: precision and recall at least the hand-executed runs' on every acceptance case
controls.outcome_recorded_in: acceptance report; the engine's inference log (one record per attempt, including refusals)
controls.monitored_by: GitHub Actions `validate.yml` on every push and pull request (Python 3.10–3.12); a failure marks the commit red; tests/test_acceptance.py

controls.control: Engine output is always `proposed`, valid, never re-proposes an approved link, never names a record that does not exist
controls.monitored_by: GitHub Actions `validate.yml` on every push and pull request (Python 3.10–3.12); a failure marks the commit red; tests/test_acceptance.py

controls.control: Every entity, link row, link type, rule and attribute names its source, reasoning and confidence
controls.monitored_by: GitHub Actions `validate.yml` on every push and pull request (Python 3.10–3.12); a failure marks the commit red

controls.control: Every confidence rating follows the single confidence rule
controls.monitored_by: GitHub Actions `validate.yml` on every push and pull request (Python 3.10–3.12); a failure marks the commit red

controls.control: Every generated document, diagram and schema matches the records
controls.monitored_by: GitHub Actions `validate.yml` on every push and pull request (Python 3.10–3.12); a failure marks the commit red

controls.control: The owner's high-level metamodel specification is unchanged
controls.monitored_by: GitHub Actions `validate.yml` on every push and pull request (Python 3.10–3.12); a failure marks the commit red

controls.control: A graph store is only written from data that passes every check; a failed build keeps the last good store; every build is logged
controls.outcome_recorded_in: the store's `load-record.json` (accepted / rejected, inputs with checksums, errors, warnings, outputs)
controls.monitored_by: GitHub Actions `validate.yml` on every push and pull request (Python 3.10–3.12); a failure marks the commit red (build --check on every example store); tests/test_store.py

controls.control: A projected design (AID) never enters an architecture dataset, the Relationship Registry or a real graph store, and a projected link is never approved
controls.implemented_in: sdem/graph.py `LevelGraph.validate` (dataset check), sdem/validate.py (registry validator), sdem/store.py `render` (store build): reject `PRJ-`/`DSN-` records in real datasets, approval of links to them, and projection or target-design datasets in a real store
controls.outcome_recorded_in: command output; graph store load record
controls.monitored_by: GitHub Actions `validate.yml` on every push and pull request; tests/test_use_case_example_2.py

controls.control: Every projected element carries its projection provenance, is never above medium confidence (never above low when its evidence is name-only), and never invents a BIAN element
controls.implemented_in: `schema/projection.schema.json` and sdem/aid.py `check` — run by `sdem-aid project` before writing, and by `sdem-aid check`
controls.monitored_by: GitHub Actions `validate.yml` on every push and pull request; tests/test_use_case_example_2.py

gaps.not_controlled: How each rule matches lives in the engine's code; nothing checks it against the rule's description in the rulebook
gaps.risk: the rulebook and the engine could drift apart; only CTL-09 would notice

gaps.not_controlled: Each link type's limit (one-to-many …) is recorded but not checked
gaps.risk: none today — all 9 types are many-to-many
